definitions.gloss: to hold back, to stop, to detain
definitions.explanation: To prevent someone from leaving or going somewhere.

definitions.gloss: to dissuade, to talk out of
definitions.explanation: To persuade someone not to do something, especially resigning or quitting.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}が{帰|かえ}ろうとしたので{引|ひ}き{止|と}めた。
examples.english: My friend was about to leave, so I held them back.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{辞職|じしょく}を{何|なん}とか{引|ひ}き{止|と}めたい。
examples.english: I want to somehow talk him out of resigning.

examples.japanese: {暴走|ぼうそう}する{車|くるま}を{引|ひ}き{止|と}めることはできなかった。
examples.english: It was impossible to stop the runaway car.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}は{優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{社員|しゃいん}を{引|ひ}き{止|と}めるために{給料|きゅうりょう}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The president raised salaries to retain talented employees.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Compound verb: {引|ひ}く + {止|と}める. Pattern: Xを{引|ひ}き{止|と}める (hold back X / stop X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing effort. {引|ひ}き{止|と}めている = 'is trying to hold back' or 'is detaining.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{人|ひと}を{引|ひ}き{止|と}める (hold someone back)
・{辞職|じしょく}を{引|ひ}き{止|と}める (talk someone out of resigning)
・{何|なん}とか{引|ひ}き{止|と}める (somehow try to stop/retain)

NOTE: Often used in workplace contexts when trying to prevent someone from quitting. Can also be written as {引|ひ}き{留|と}める with the same meaning.
